```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  cache = FALSE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

Observer programmes rarely sample all vessels equally. Some vessels are sampled
in every season, others only sporadically, and the mix of observed vessels
changes from year to year. Because vessels differ in the size-composition of
their catch — through gear configuration, skipper behaviour, or preferred
fishing grounds — the raw observer sample can be a poor representation of the
fleet-wide catch composition.

This vignette demonstrates how `ComPoM` can correct for vessel-level sampling
bias using a Poisson-multinomial model fitted with either a Bayesian backend
(`brms`) or a frequentist random-effects backend (`sdmTMB` without a mesh).
Neither model uses spatial information; instead, both treat vessel identity and
season as crossed random effects interacting with the composition bins.

The simulation generates a fleet of vessels with vessel-specific selectivity
offsets and year/season effects, then samples that fleet unevenly — a small
subset of vessels is heavily over-represented, and their seasonal coverage
shifts across years. We compare three approaches for estimating fleet-wide
catch compositions:

1. **Raw scaled samples** — naively treating observer data as representative
2. **sdmTMB (non-spatial)** — maximum-likelihood Poisson-multinomial with
   random effects
3. **brms (Bayesian)** — fully Bayesian Poisson-multinomial with the same
   random-effect structure

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(ComPoM)
library(sdmTMB)

source("vignette_helpers.R")

clo <- function(x) x / sum(x)

# Simulation parameters
n_bins <- 10
n_vessels <- 40
n_seasons <- 4
n_years <- 8
n_samps_per_year <- 60
n_per_samp <- 100

# Population and selectivity
M <- 0.2
surv <- exp(-(1:n_bins) * M)
popfreq <- clo(surv)

L50_base <- 6.5
L95 <- 0.75
```

## Simulate Fleet

Each vessel has a persistent selectivity offset drawn from a normal
distribution — some vessels catch larger fish, others smaller.

Figure 1 shows the simulated vessel offsets.

```{r simulate-fleet, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 1. Simulated vessel-specific offsets of log(L50).
set.seed(42)

vessels <- tibble(
  vessel_id = factor(1:n_vessels),
  vessel_effect = rnorm(n_vessels, 0, 0.3)
)

ggplot(vessels, aes(x = vessel_id, y = vessel_effect)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = function(x) x[seq(1, length(x), by = 5)]) +
  labs(x = "Vessel", y = "Effect on log(L50)")
```

## Simulate Temporal and Seasonal Effects

```{r simulate-temporal}
year_effects <- cumsum(rnorm(n_years, 0, 0.1))
year_effects <- year_effects - mean(year_effects)

season_effects <- rnorm(n_seasons, 0, 0.2)
season_effects <- season_effects - mean(season_effects)

temporal_df <- expand_grid(
  Year = factor(1:n_years),
  Season = factor(1:n_seasons)
) |>
  mutate(
    year_effect = year_effects[as.integer(Year)],
    season_effect = season_effects[as.integer(Season)]
  )
```

## Generate True Catch Compositions

The true fleet-wide composition integrates over all vessels, years, and
seasons.

```{r true-catch}
true_catch_by_bin <- expand_grid(
  vessel_id = factor(1:n_vessels),
  Year = factor(1:n_years),
  Season = factor(1:n_seasons),
  bin = 1:n_bins
) |>
  left_join(vessels, by = "vessel_id") |>
  left_join(temporal_df, by = c("Year", "Season")) |>
  mutate(
    L50 = exp(log(L50_base) + vessel_effect + year_effect + season_effect),
    catch = rgamma(n(), 100, 0.01),
    tcatch = Selectivity(bin, L50, L95) * popfreq[bin] * catch
  )

true_comp_year <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(Year, bin) |>
  summarise(tcatch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")
```

## Simulate Non-Representative Sampling

Sampling is biased in two ways:

- **Vessel bias**: a handful of vessels (the top 8) are sampled much more
  frequently than the rest.
- **Seasonal shift**: early years oversample season 1; late years oversample
  season 4. This mimics a programme that changes its coverage over time.

Figure 2 shows the number of trips sampled per vessel.

```{r simulate-sampling, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 2. Number of trips sampled per vessel.
# Vessel sampling weights — top 8 vessels get 5x the weight
vessel_weights <- rep(1, n_vessels)
vessel_weights[1:8] <- 5
vessel_weights <- vessel_weights / sum(vessel_weights)

# Seasonal weights that shift over time
season_probs_by_year <- function(year, n_years, n_seasons) {
  alpha <- (year - 1) / (n_years - 1)
  weights <- rep(0.5, n_seasons)
  weights[1] <- 4 * (1 - alpha) + 0.5 * alpha
  weights[n_seasons] <- 0.5 * (1 - alpha) + 4 * alpha
  weights / sum(weights)
}


samples <- tibble(
  samp_id = 1:(n_samps_per_year * n_years),
  Year = factor(rep(1:n_years, each = n_samps_per_year))
) |>
  mutate(
    vessel_id = factor(sample(1:n_vessels, n(), replace = TRUE, prob = vessel_weights)),
    Season = factor(sapply(as.integer(Year), function(yr) {
      sample(1:n_seasons, 1, prob = season_probs_by_year(yr, n_years, n_seasons))
    }))
  ) |>
  left_join(vessels, by = "vessel_id") |>
  left_join(temporal_df, by = c("Year", "Season")) |>
  mutate(
    L50 = exp(log(L50_base) + vessel_effect + year_effect + season_effect)
  )

# Generate composition samples
long_form_sims <- samples |>
  group_by(samp_id) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    comp_samps = lapply(data, function(df) {
      which(rmultinom(n_per_samp, 1,
                      Selectivity(1:n_bins, df$L50, L95) * popfreq) == 1,
            arr.ind = TRUE)[, 1]
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(c(data, comp_samps)) |>
  mutate(count = 1) |>
  rename(bin = comp_samps)

# Visualise sampling bias
sampling_summary <- long_form_sims |>
  distinct(samp_id, vessel_id, Year, Season) |>
  count(vessel_id, name = "n_trips")

ggplot(sampling_summary, aes(x = vessel_id, y = n_trips)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = function(x) x[seq(1, length(x), by = 5)]) +
  labs(x = "Vessel", y = "Trips sampled")
```

Figure 3 shows the number of samples per season in each year.

```{r sampling-by-season, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 3. Number of samples per season in each year.
season_summary <- long_form_sims |>
  distinct(samp_id, Year, Season) |>
  count(Year, Season)

ggplot(season_summary, aes(x = Season, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  facet_wrap(~Year, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Season", y = "Samples")
```

## Prepare Data

```{r prepare-data}
input_data <- data_prep(
  long_form_sims,
  vars_for_grouping = c("vessel_id", "Year", "Season"),
  bin_lab = "bin"
)
```

## Fit Non-Spatial sdmTMB Model

```{r fit-tmb}
mod_tmb <- fit_model(
  re_form = "Season + vessel_id",
  ffx_form = "Year",
  data = input_data,
  backend = "TMB",
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  thin = 2
)
```

## Fit Bayesian Model with brms

```{r fit-brms, message=FALSE}
mod_brms <- fit_model(
  re_form = "Season + vessel_id",
  ffx_form = "Year",
  data = input_data,
  backend = "brms",
  dist=poisson(),
  brms_backend = "rstan",
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  thin = 2
)
```

## Effects Plots

Figure 4 shows the year and season effects from both models.

```{r effects, fig.dim=c(14, 12)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 4. Year effects (a, b) and season effects (c, d) on the composition, as multipliers relative to
#|   the geometric mean across bins, from the sdmTMB model (a, c) and the brms model (b, d).
#|   Points are medians and bars 95% intervals.
(Fx_plot(mod_tmb, grp = "Year", grid = NULL) |
   Fx_plot(mod_brms, grp = "Year", grid = NULL)) /
  (Fx_plot(mod_tmb, grp = "Season", grid = NULL) |
     Fx_plot(mod_brms, grp = "Season", grid = NULL)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Scale Compositions to Catch

Predictions from each model were scaled to the true catch by year, season and
vessel (catch weighting, `mode = "catch"`) and then aggregated to
annual compositions. Catch weighting evaluates the nuisance random effects (season
and vessel) at the level of each stratum, so both variables must be in `grps`.
The result estimates the composition of the total catch of the fleet.

```{r scale-compositions}
# Scaling data: total catch by year, season and vessel (full fleet)
scale_df <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(Year, Season, vessel_id) |>
  summarise(catch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")

scaled_tmb <- scale_comps(
  scale_df,
  predvar = "catch",
  fit = mod_tmb,
  grps = c("Year", "Season", "vessel_id")
)

scaled_brms <- scale_comps(
  scale_df,
  predvar = "catch",
  fit = mod_brms,
  grps = c("Year", "Season", "vessel_id")
)

# Aggregate to annual
scaled_tmb_yr <- scaled_tmb |>
  group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

scaled_brms_yr <- scaled_brms |>
  group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")
```

## Compare Scaled Compositions to Truth

Figure 5 shows the scaled annual compositions against the true composition.

```{r compare-truth, fig.dim=c(10, 14)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 5. Annual compositions of the catch from the sdmTMB model (a) and the brms model (b). Black
#|   points and bars are medians and 95% intervals, and skyblue points the true composition.
p_truth_tmb <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_tmb_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  cvar = "tcatch",
  comp_label = "True"
)

p_truth_brms <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_brms_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  cvar = "tcatch",
  comp_label = "True"
)

p_truth_tmb / p_truth_brms + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Evaluate Against Raw Samples

```{r raw-comp}
raw_comp <- input_data |>
  group_by(Year, bin) |>
  summarise(tcatch = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")
```

Figure 6 shows the scaled compositions together with the true and raw sample compositions.

```{r compare-raw, fig.dim=c(10, 14)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 6. Annual compositions from the sdmTMB model (a) and the brms model (b), with the true
#|   composition (skyblue) and the raw sample composition (orange). Black points and bars are
#|   medians and 95% intervals.
p_raw_tmb <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_tmb_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = "tcatch",
  comp_label = "True",
  comp2_label = "Raw samples"
)

p_raw_brms <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_brms_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = "tcatch",
  comp_label = "True",
  comp2_label = "Raw samples"
)

p_raw_tmb / p_raw_brms + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Ridgeline Plots of Scaled Compositions

Ridgeline plots show the modelled size composition by year.
`scaled_ridge_plot()` takes the output of `scale_comps()` directly; `plot_y`
sets the variable stacked on the y-axis and `plot_facet` optionally splits the
display across a second variable (here, not needed as we are already aggregated
to annual).

Figure 7 shows the annual compositions as ridgelines.

```{r ridge, fig.dim=c(12, 7)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 7. Annual size compositions (ridgelines) from the sdmTMB model (a) and the brms model (b).
library(ggridges)

p_ridge_tmb <- scaled_ridge_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_tmb_yr,
  grps        = "Year",
  plot_y      = "Year"
)

p_ridge_brms <- scaled_ridge_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_brms_yr,
  grps        = "Year",
  plot_y      = "Year"
)

(p_ridge_tmb | p_ridge_brms) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

If you have a second grouping variable (e.g. season within year) you can pass
it to `plot_facet` to produce a faceted ridgeline display:

Figure 8 shows the sdmTMB compositions by season.

```{r ridge-tmb-season, fig.dim=c(10, 8)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 8. Annual size compositions (ridgelines) from the sdmTMB model by season.
# Re-aggregate retaining Season
scaled_tmb_yr_season <- scaled_tmb |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year, Season, bin, .draw) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

scaled_ridge_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_tmb_yr_season,
  grps        = c("Year", "Season"),
  plot_y      = "Year",
  plot_facet  = "Season"
)
```

## Relative Error Comparison

Figure 9 shows the relative error of the models and of the raw samples.

```{r relative-error, fig.dim=c(10, 5)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 9. Relative error of the annual proportions from the sdmTMB model (a) and the brms model (b),
#|   compared with the relative error of the raw samples, against the true composition.
p_err_tmb <- scaled_comp_comp(
  scaled_comp = scaled_tmb_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = "tcatch"
)

p_err_brms <- scaled_comp_comp(
  scaled_comp = scaled_brms_yr,
  grps = "Year",
  scaled = TRUE,
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = "tcatch"
)

(p_err_tmb | p_err_brms) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

Both the Bayesian and the frequentist model recovered the true fleet-wide
compositions with lower relative error than the raw samples. The median relative
error was about 0.035 for both models and 0.058 for the raw samples.

## Influence of Model Terms

The influence functions refit the sdmTMB model and therefore do not apply to the brms fit. Figure 10
shows the mean length of the annual composition when the terms were added to the model one at a
time (`step_comps()`), for the catch component (`mode = "catch"`) and for the index component
(`mode = "index"`). The first step was the model with bin-specific intercepts only, which gives the
same composition in every year. In the index component, season and vessel were selectivity terms
and were set to the population level.

```{r step, fig.dim=c(10, 5)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 10. Mean length of the annual composition (with 95% intervals) as terms were added to
#|   the sdmTMB model, for the catch component (top row) and the index component (bottom row). The
#|   current step is orange, the previous step skyblue and earlier steps grey.
index_grid <- dplyr::distinct(scale_df, Year)

steps <- step_comps(
  mod_tmb,
  scale_df = scale_df, predvar = "catch",
  grps = c("Year", "Season", "vessel_id"), by = "Year",
  grid = index_grid
)
plot_step_comps(steps)
```

```{r step-numbers, include = FALSE}
step_mean <- function(comp, st) {
  steps$steps |> dplyr::filter(component == comp, step == st) |> dplyr::arrange(level) |> dplyr::pull(mean)
}
shift_vessel <- sapply(c("catch", "index"), function(cmp)
  mean(step_mean(cmp, "+ vessel_id") - step_mean(cmp, "+ Season")))
shift_season <- sapply(c("catch", "index"), function(cmp)
  mean(step_mean(cmp, "+ Season") - step_mean(cmp, "+ Year")))
```

Adding the year effect produced the trend in mean length. Adding season changed the mean length
by `r sprintf("%.3f", shift_season["catch"])` on average in the catch component. Adding vessel changed it by
`r sprintf("%.3f", shift_vessel["catch"])` in the catch component and by `r sprintf("%.3f", shift_vessel["index"])`
in the index component.

`influ_comps()` summarises the effect of a term on each bin. With the TMB backend, the two random
effects can only be removed together, so season and vessel form one term. Figures 11 and 12 show
the levels of vessel and of season for that term. In each figure, the top panel shows the effect of
each level on every length bin, as the log of the multiplier relative to the geometric mean over
levels. The centre panel shows the share of the catch in each level and year, and the right panel
shows the influence of the term on the annual composition, as the log ratio of the proportion in
each bin with and without the term. The levels (x) are shared between the top and centre panels, and
the years (y) between the centre and right panels. Cells whose 95% interval includes zero are
faded. The influence is shown for the catch component. The index component has no influence of
these terms, because they were set to the population level.

```{r influence}
influence <- influ_comps(
  mod_tmb,
  scale_df = scale_df, predvar = "catch",
  grps = c("Year", "Season", "vessel_id"), by = "Year",
  grid = index_grid, components = "catch"
)
re_term <- names(influence$groups)
max_infl <- max(abs(dplyr::filter(influence$influence, component == "catch")$mean))
max_eff <- tapply(abs(influence$effects$effect), influence$effects$var, max)
```

```{r cdi-vessel, fig.dim=c(10, 8)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 11. Effect of each vessel on each length bin (top), share of the catch by vessel and
#|   year (centre) and influence of the random effects on the annual composition (right).
plot_cdi_comps(influence, re_term, var = "vessel_id", component = "catch")
```

```{r cdi-season, fig.dim=c(10, 8)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 12. As Figure 11, for season.
plot_cdi_comps(influence, re_term, var = "Season", component = "catch")
```

The largest absolute effect of a level on a bin was `r sprintf("%.2f", max_eff["vessel_id"])` for vessel and
`r sprintf("%.2f", max_eff["Season"])` for season on the log scale. The largest absolute influence of the random effects on any bin and year was
`r sprintf("%.2f", max_infl)` on the log scale. The influence was similar in all years, because the
shares of the catch by vessel and season were similar in all years (centre panels).
